chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Barqi from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sayyabah said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Tawaf (circumambulation), and I said: 'Do I hurry and increase (steps) or walk and slow down?' He said, 'Walking is between the two extremes.'

And whoever circumambulates the House with six Shaws (circuits) and departs, let him add one more Shaw, and there is no penalty upon him. If he does not remember until he returns to his family, he shall order someone to circumambulate on his behalf.

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: Shaws (singular: Shawt), circuits or rounds of Tawaf
key_terms.بَيْنَ الْمَشْيَيْنِ: Between the two walks (moderate pace between hurrying and slowing)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper walking pace for Tawaf and what if I only complete six circuits?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the ideal Tawaf pace as 'walking between the two walks,' balancing the brisk 'Haml' of the first three circuits with the slower, contemplative pace of the last four. This hadith also clarifies the flexibility in completing the ritual, allowing for a simple addition of one circuit if only six are performed, or delegating the completion to another if the pilgrim has already departed, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and practicality in worship.
